About:

PRLX is a solo team focused on turning complex spatial data into smooth, interactive experiences. As a software engineer, I enjoy building tools that operate at the intersection of raw data and visual performance.

Team Status: 

Working independently to execute a specific technical proof-of-concept. Not looking for additional members.
summary:
PRLX is an interactive Mars surface navigation and EVA mission-planning platform built on real 1-meter NASA HiRISE Digital Terrain Models (DTM) across four landing zones: Jezero Delta, Gale Boxwork, Candor Chasma, and Oxia Planum.

Instead of relying on static maps, PRLX lets mission planners and astronauts place custom waypoints directly on the Martian globe. A terrain-aware A* pathfinder evaluates full 2D slope gradients to avoid steep cliffs and sharp descents, routing traverses safely along flat valley floors while calculating elevation profiles, UHF radio line-of-sight obstructions, and oxygen consumption. Users can switch between four real-time data layers — Optical, Topography & Slope, USGS Geology, and Radiation/Dune Hazards — and drop directly into a first-person 3D surface POV simulator with Martian gravity (3.72 m/s²), a player-centered tactical map, and live terrain telemetry.

PRLX bridges orbital planetary data and on-the-ground astronaut safety, turning complex Martian elevation datasets into actionable, life-saving traverse decisions.
details:
How It Works

PRLX is a 3D Martian mission-planning and EVA simulation platform. Users explore four landing zones (Jezero Delta, Gale Boxwork, Candor Chasma, Oxia Planum) across four orbital layers (Optical, Topography & Slope, Geology USGS, Hazards & Radiation), place waypoints, and generate safe routes using a 108x108 A* pathfinder on 1m HiRISE terrain data. The planner accounts for 2D terrain slopes (20 deg On Foot, 15 deg Rover), valley-floor radiation shielding (8-ray horizon check), UHF Line-of-Sight, O2 usage, and crisis modes (Nominal, SPE Storm, Dust Storm). Users can then drop into a Three.js first-person 3D POV with Martian gravity (3.72 m/s^2), a tactical minimap, waypoint inspection, and JSON export.

Benefits & Impact

PRLX turns complex planetary GIS data into an accessible tactical simulator, helping researchers, students, and mission planners design safer human/rover traverses and test emergency routing under space-weather hazards.

Tools & Data

TypeScript, React, Sass, Vite, ArcGIS Maps SDK for JS (Mars 2000 WKID 104971), Three.js, NASA/JPL HiRISE 1m DTM, USGS MDIM 2.1, USGS Geology & Dune databases, and NASA DONKI Space Weather API (built on the open-source Esri/explore-mars Apache 2.0 base).

Creativity & Key Factors

Instead of a static 2D map, PRLX connects orbital planning directly to a real-time 3D surface simulation, balancing shortest path against slope safety, terrain radiation cover, and radio visibility.
